subject: Re: Follow-up — Pricing and Batching assumptions (Helium Labs)
messages:
From: camila_reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@helium.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-15T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Pricing + batching assumptions from today’s call

Hi Liam — great to meet earlier. Quick recap and a few items we need to firm up to size pricing: 

Summary of what you shared:
- Workload: conversational assistant for customer support (avg. 1.2k tokens in prompt + 200 tokens response).
- Traffic: ~450k monthly active users, ~15% MAU daily; estimate ~1.2M requests/month initially.
- Real-time SLA: sub-300ms tail for core happy-path queries.
- Ops pattern: steady traffic with daily peaks 10:00–14:00 PT; you expect continuous batching to be effective because requests are spread across many users and you can tolerate <50ms additional queuing.

Open items we need from you to produce target pricing and unit-econ: 
1) Confirm total monthly token volume estimate (prompt+response) or per-day distribution if easier.
2) Target budget range for hosted API + dedicated options (ballpark $/month).
3) Any strict latency SLOs per route (so we can propose continuous batching window & concurrency).
4) Are there any data retention/compliance needs that push away hosted and toward Dedicated/Private?

Initial assumptions we used on-call: continuous batching scenario with 100–300ms batching window, average effective batching factor 4–8x for your traffic pattern; concurrency per model replica estimated at 40 in that config. We’ll run a quick econ calc once you confirm token volumes.

Attaching a short Mutual Action Plan that outlines next steps + a pricing worksheet draft. Can you send the token volume numbers (daily or monthly) and your target $/1M tokens if you have a target? Even a range is fine.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Mutual_Action_Plan_Helium_Redwood.xlsx, Redwood_Pricing_Batching_Notes.pdf

From: Liam O'Connor <liam@helium.ai>
To: camila_reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-17T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Pricing + batching assumptions from today’s call

Thanks Camila — great summary. A few clarifications: 

1) Token volumes: we ran a quick back-of-envelope from product metrics: avg tokens/request ~1.4k (prompt+resp). Expected ramp: Month1 ~1.2M requests, Month3 ~3.6M requests (we're planning a staged roll-out). So Month1 tokens ~1.68B, Month3 ~5.04B.

2) Budget: for hosted API we have ~$8k–$12k/mo top of funnel but could commit more if unit economics work (target would be <$80 per 1M tokens to start, ideally $50–$70/1M as we scale). For a Dedicated contract, we could discuss a monthly commit in the $40k–$60k range if it buys predictable latency and cost.

3) Latency SLOs: 95th tail <350ms is required for core flow; best-effort for other routes.

4) Compliance: no strict on-prem requirement today; SOC2 and audit logs are needed.

Happy to hop on a quick follow-up call this week to go through the worksheet.

— Liam
Head of Product, Helium Labs
liam@helium.ai | +1 650-555-2044

From: camila_reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@helium.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T11:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Pricing + batching assumptions from today’s call

Thanks Liam — super helpful. Based on your numbers I put together a short unit-econ outline and a couple of configuration options (high-level):

Option A — Hosted (fastest time-to-value)
- Assumptions: avg tokens/request 1.4k, Month1 1.68B tokens, Month3 5.04B tokens.
- Pricing bands (illustrative): $120 / 1M tokens for smaller volume bands, stepping down to $60 / 1M above ~4B tokens.
- Continuous batching: we expect effective batching factor ~5x on your traffic with a 150–250ms batching window, which drives token-unit-cost down.
- Pros: no infra to manage, quick to start.
- Cons: higher unit price at small volumes, limited custom kernel tuning.

Option B — Dedicated (reserved capacity)
- Assumptions: 40–60% cost savings on token unit once you hit predictable commit (depends on model choice & quantization).
- Pricing: modeled as a committed monthly fee ($40k–$60k) + lower per-token overage (e.g., $30–$50 / 1M tokens depending on commit).
- Continuous batching & concurrency: with Dedicated we can configure replicas with higher concurrency and longer batching windows where acceptable, raising batching factor to 6–10x for your spread workload.
- Pros: predictable economics and SLA control.

Key tradeoffs to confirm from you:
- What fallback latency (extra queuing) is acceptable for non-core queries? That lets us recommend a batching window per route.
- Is your deployment tolerant of sub-300ms additional queuing for a 5x cost win?

Next steps I propose: 
1) You confirm Month1 and Month3 token numbers (you gave requests; I converted to tokens above) and pick a target $/1M token range you want us to optimize to (e.g., $50–$70).
2) We run a model-level econ calc + propose hosted vs dedicated with exact numbers (I’ll include sensitivity to batching factor).
3) Quick follow-up call to walk through the Mutual Action Plan and timeline.

I attached the pricing worksheet and Mutual Action Plan — I’ll update with your confirmed tokens and budget and send a follow-up by EOD after our call.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Pricing + batching assumptions from today’s call

Looping in a quick note — Camila, happy to support pricing sensitivity. Two things from ops/sales motion: 
- If Helium prioritizes 95th <350ms we should quantify how much headroom that leaves for batching. My estimate: for core route we can allow only a ~100ms batching window (lower batching factor), but move other non-core routes to 200–300ms windows.
- For the Dedicated math, I can draft a commit-tier proposal that maps $/1M tokens to commit bands. Will take your worksheet as input.

Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
